questions.question: Medium 1 has the electrical permittivity [latex]\varepsilon _{1}=1.5\varepsilon _{0}[/latex] farad/m and occupies the region to the left of x = 0 plane. Medium 2 has the electrical permittivity [latex]\varepsilon _{2}=2.5\varepsilon _{0}[/latex] farad/m and occupies the region to the right of x = 0 plane. If [latex]E_{1}[/latex] in medium 1 is [latex]E_{1}[/latex] = [latex](2u_{x}-3u_{y}+1u_{z})[/latex] volt/m, then  [latex]E_{2}[/latex] in medium 2 is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \vec{E}_{1} &=2 u_{x}-3 u_{y}+1 u_{z} \\ \vec{E}_{1 t} &=-3 u_{y}+u_{z}=E_{2 t} &(x=0 \text { plane}) \\ \vec{E}_{1 n} &=2 u_{x} \\ \vec{D}_{1 n} &=\vec{D}_{2 n}=\epsilon \vec{E} \\ \Rightarrow \epsilon_{1} \vec{E}_{1 n} &=\epsilon_{2} \vec{E}_{2 n} \\ &=1.5 \epsilon_{0} \cdot 2 u_{x}=2.5 \epsilon_{0} \cdot \vec{E}_{2 n} \\ \vec{E}_{2 n} &=\frac{3}{2.5} u_{x}=1.2 u_{x} \\ \vec{E}_{2} &=\vec{E}_{2 t}+\vec{E}_{2 n} \\ \vec{E}_{2} &=-3 u_{y}+u_{z}+1.2 u_{x} \\ &=1.2u_{x}-3.0u_{y}+1.0u_{z} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} \vec{E}_{1} &=2 u_{x}-3 u_{y}+1 u_{z} \\ \vec{E}_{1 t} &=-3 u_{y}+u_{z}=E_{2 t} &(x=0 \text { plane}) \\ \vec{E}_{1 n} &=2 u_{x} \\ \vec{D}_{1 n} &=\vec{D}_{2 n}=\epsilon \vec{E} \\ \Rightarrow \epsilon_{1} \vec{E}_{1 n} &=\epsilon_{2} \vec{E}_{2 n} \\ &=1.5 \epsilon_{0} \cdot 2 u_{x}=2.5 \epsilon_{0} \cdot \vec{E}_{2 n} \\ \vec{E}_{2 n} &=\frac{3}{2.5} u_{x}=1.2 u_{x} \\ \vec{E}_{2} &=\vec{E}_{2 t}+\vec{E}_{2 n} \\ \vec{E}_{2} &=-3 u_{y}+u_{z}+1.2 u_{x} \\ &=1.2u_{x}-3.0u_{y}+1.0u_{z} \end{aligned}[/latex]
